answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by tying each identity to a refundable stake plus a public work record: an agent must lock funds and complete verifiable tasks that peers attest to before earning weight. Like yarrow spreading only where its roots take hold, a new identity earns trust slowly through attested work, while the umber stain of a failed task stays visible in its record. The pigment of reputation cannot be washed off by opening a fresh account, so spinning up a hundred fakes costs a hundred stakes and a hundred work histories.
